Titan Industrial Equipment Corp. - Q3 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Titan Industrial Equipment Corp. Q3 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. To ask a question, you will need to press star one on your touchtone phone. To withdraw your question, press star two. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson (Head of Investor Relations):
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Titan Industrial Equipment Corp.'s results for the Q3. Joining me on today's call are Mark Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Financial Officer; David Ramirez, Chief Operating Officer; and Dr. Elena Vasquez, Chief Technology Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking in nature and subject to certain risks and uncertainties. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Mark Thompson.

Mark Thompson (CEO):
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. I'm pleased to report on Titan Industrial Equipment Corp.'s performance for the Q3. We've made significant progress on several fronts, and I'd like to highlight a few key achievements. We've issued strong operating margin guidance for the next quarter and full year, reflecting disciplined execution amid solid core segment performance. Demand trends across our key end markets like construction, mining, agriculture, and manufacturing remain robust, with backlog growth underscoring multi-year tailwinds. Total order intake hit record levels with impressive year-over-year growth, driven by core equipment and aftermarket strength. Our share repurchase program is executing opportunistically, delivering meaningful EPS accretion. Order intake expectations point to continued momentum, paired with strong backlog conversion rates thanks to supply chain improvements. Automation and digital offerings are accelerating growth while boosting efficiency for us and our customers. Finally, the outlook for end market growth looks resilient in the near term and accelerating in the medium term.

We are confident that our strategic initiatives are positioning us for long-term sustainable growth.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Lisa Chen to provide more detail on our financial results.

Lisa Chen (CFO):
Thank you, Mark. Turning to our financial performance, Titan Industrial Equipment Corp. reported $7.2 billion in revenue for the Q3, representing a 16% increase year-over-year. Gross margin was 28.5%, driven by a higher mix of aftermarket parts and services, favorable pricing actions, and productivity gains from our manufacturing facilities. Operating expenses were $1.15 billion, resulting in an operating income of $825 million. Our net income for the quarter was $620 million, or $4.15 per share.

As we turn to forward guidance, I'd like to provide some color on our operating margin outlook for the fourth quarter and the full fiscal year 2024. We're guiding to an operating margin of 13.5% to 14.5% for Q4, representing a modest sequential decline from our Q3 realized margin of 14.2%, but still within our historical range for a seasonally softer quarter. For the full year, we're narrowing our guidance to 14.0% to 14.5%, up from our prior range of 13.5% to 14.5%, reflecting the strength we've seen in our core segments and proactive margin management.

Let me break this down by the key drivers, starting with the revenue side. We're expecting Q4 organic growth of 8-10% year-over-year, driven by a rebound in capital equipment orders for automation systems—particularly our next-gen FlexArm robotic welders and PrecisionCNC milling centers, which saw a 25% bookings surge in Q3 from automotive OEMs like Ford and GM reshoring stamping and assembly lines under the CHIPS Act tailwinds. Aftermarket parts and services, which now represent 32% of total revenue—up from 28% two years ago—should contribute another 150 basis points of margin expansion through higher-margin predictive maintenance contracts powered by our AI-Driven TitanSense platform. This mirrors trends we've seen at peers like Rockwell Automation, where digital services have boosted EBITDA margins by 200-300 bps over the past 18 months.

However, we're baking in some near-term margin pressure from input cost inflation and strategic investments. Raw material costs, especially high-strength steel and aluminum alloys critical for our heavy-duty AeroForge presses and HydroLift material handling systems, remain volatile—up 5-7% quarter-over-quarter due to lingering supply chain disruptions from the Red Sea rerouting and domestic tariff uncertainties on Chinese imports. We've hedged 70% of our FY24 exposure, but unhedged spot pricing could shave 50-75 bps off margins if steel benchmarks like the CRU North American Hot-Rolled Coil Index stays above $750/ton. Labor costs are another headwind; skilled machinists and PLC programmers command 6-8% wage premiums amid U.S. manufacturing PMI hovering at 48-50, prompting us to accelerate automation in our own plants—similar to Caterpillar's playbook with their autonomous mining equipment rollout.

Regionally, the Americas will be our margin anchor, targeting 16-17% sub-regional operating margins on 12% growth, fueled by megatrends like nearshoring to Mexico and data center buildouts requiring our ModuRack storage automation solutions. Europe faces headwinds with expected 2-4% margins due to softening industrial capex—German machine tool orders down 15% YoY per VDW data—and elevated energy costs post-Ukraine fallout, though our energy-efficient EcoDrive servo motors are gaining traction with Siemens and Bosch for retrofits. In Asia-Pacific, we'll see flattish 10-12% margins amid China stimulus boosting short-cycle CNC demand, offset by pricing pressure from local competitors like Shenyang Machine Tool; we're countering this with localized production in our new Pune, India facility, which ramps to 20% utilization in Q4.

Strategically, we're laser-focused on operational leverage through our MarginPlus 2025 initiative, which includes three pillars: first, supply chain resilience—diversifying from 40% China-sourced components to 60/40 North America/India by year-end, reducing lead times by 25% and FX exposure; second, digital transformation—scaling our TitanForge digital twin software across 40% of our installed base, driving 300 bps of gross margin uplift via virtual prototyping that cuts physical prototyping costs by 30%, akin to Hexagon AB's success; and third, sustainability investments—$50 million capex for electric arc furnace recycling in our foundries to meet EU CBAM tariffs and U.S. IRA incentives, positioning us for green steel equipment demand from Nucor and Steel Dynamics.

Absorption remains strong at 92% across our 12 U.S. and Mexican plants, with fixed cost leverage adding 100 bps to margins as we exit Q4. SG&A as a percent of sales should decline to 9.5-10.0% from 10.2% in Q3, thanks to zero-based budgeting and shared services synergies from last year's acquisition of RoboTech Dynamics, which is already delivering 50 bps of accretion.

Before diving deeper into the numbers, I'd like to provide some color on demand trends across our core end markets: construction, mining, agriculture, and manufacturing. Overall, we saw robust demand in Q3, with our equipment backlog growing 18% year-over-year to $12.4 billion, reflecting a book-to-bill ratio of 1.35x. This strength is driven by a mix of cyclical recovery, secular tailwinds like electrification and digitalization, and resilient aftermarket support, which now accounts for 42% of our total revenues—up from 38% last year.

Starting with construction, which represents about 35% of our sales mix, demand remains solid but differentiated by sub-segment. Non-residential construction, particularly infrastructure-related, continues to outperform, fueled by record U.S. federal spending under the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act (IIJA). We've seen U.S. highway and bridge capex surge 22% YoY, translating to a 15% increase in our North American excavator and wheel loader orders. Globally, our hydraulic excavator shipments grew 12% QoQ, with mid-sized models like our ZX490LC-7 seeing particular strength due to their fuel efficiency and telematics integration.

Residential construction softened slightly with U.S. housing starts down 8% YoY amid high interest rates, pressuring compact track loader demand. In Europe, the EU's Green Deal is accelerating demand for low-emission equipment, where our Stage V-compliant dozers captured 14% market share in EMEA, up from 11% last year. APAC, led by India’s infrastructure push, delivered a standout 25% YoY order growth for our off-highway dump trucks, bolstered by the $1.4 trillion National Infrastructure Pipeline.

Strategically, we're leaning into sustainability with our ElectriFlex initiative—pilot programs for battery-electric excavators in partnership with Volvo CE peers, targeting 20% of construction sales to be hybrid or electric by 2027. Aftermarket parts for our legacy fleet grew 16% in construction, underscoring the stickiness of our connected services platform, which now boasts 1.2 million active telematics units.

Mining, our largest end market at 28% of revenues, posted exceptional results with a 24% YoY increase in large mining truck orders, driven by the copper and lithium supercycle. Copper prices averaging $4.50/lb in Q3—up 15% YoY—spurred greenfield projects in Chile and Australia, where our 793F-class autonomous haul trucks secured $2.1 billion in backlog from majors like BHP and Rio Tinto. Iron ore demand from China’s steel mills remains resilient despite property sector headwinds, supporting a 19% rise in our APAC mining equipment shipments.

In North America, U.S. critical minerals initiatives under the Inflation Reduction Act boosted underground loader orders by 30%, with our battery-powered scooptrams gaining traction amid ESG mandates—reducing Scope 1 emissions by up to 40%. LATAM faced headwinds from permitting delays in Peru, tempering growth to 10% YoY, but our strategic pivot to Tier 4 Final ultra-class loaders mitigated this.

A key insight here: the shift to autonomous and remote-operated systems. We've deployed over 500 autonomous trucks in active fleets, delivering 15-20% productivity gains and 25% lower OPEX, per our customer ROI models. This positions us ahead of peers like Komatsu and Liebherr, with R&D investments in AI-driven fleet optimization up 35% YoY. Aftermarket penetration hit 48% in mining, driven by predictive maintenance via our MineConnect platform.

Agriculture, at 22% of our mix, showed resilience with a 14% YoY uptick in tractor and combine orders, despite uneven farm incomes. In North America, high corn and soybean prices—averaging $5.20/bushel and $13.50/bushel—supported a robust harvest season, pushing our 400+ HP tractor backlog up 17%. The U.S. Farm Bill extension is catalyzing equipment upgrades, with precision ag features like RTK GPS and autonomous steering now standard on 65% of our new ag units.

EMEA benefited from the EU Common Agricultural Policy subsidies, driving 20% growth in forage harvesters, while Brazil's soybean boom lifted LATAM sales 18%, led by our baler and sprayer lines. APAC faced weather-related softness in Australia, down 5% QoQ, but India's mechanization trend offset this with 28% growth in compact tractors.

Farmers are prioritizing uptime and efficiency: our AgriDigital suite, integrating AI yield mapping and variable-rate application, boosted attach rates to 55% and aftermarket revenues 19% YoY. Strategically, we're addressing labor shortages with semi-autonomous tractors—pilots showing 12% labor savings—and expanding our electric compact lineup for orchards, targeting a 15% market share in sustainable ag by 2026. Replacement cycles, now at 7-8 years versus the historical 10, are a multi-year tailwind.

Rounding out with manufacturing at 15% of sales, demand accelerated 21% YoY, propelled by onshoring and Industry 4.0. U.S. CHIPS Act and reshoring from China drove material handling orders up 25%, with our electric forklifts—featuring lithium-ion batteries and AGV integration—filling backlogs at warehouses for clients like Amazon and Tesla Gigafactories. In Europe, automotive OEMs like Volkswagen are ramping EV production lines, lifting our CNC machining centers and robotic welders 16%.

APAC manufacturing softened 3% due to China's export slowdown, but Mexico's nearshoring boom—maquiladoras expanding 12%—provided offset via LATAM growth. Key trend: factory automation, where our collaborative robots (cobots) and IoT-enabled presses saw 30% order growth, aligning with peers like Fanuc and ABB.

Our insight: dual-sourcing strategies are here to stay. We've invested $450 million in U.S. and Mexican capacity expansions for precision components, de-risking supply chains post-2021 disruptions. Aftermarket services, including uptime guarantees via predictive analytics, grew 22%, with 75% of our manufacturing fleet now digitally monitored.

In summary on demand, end-market demand is firing on multiple cylinders, with mining and manufacturing as growth engines and construction/ag providing stability. We expect Q4 bookings to rise another 10-12%, with full-year 2024 revenues up 16% to $28.5 billion. Regionally, North America (45% of mix) leads at +18% growth, APAC +14%, EMEA +11%, and LATAM +13%.

Strategically, we're allocating 8% of revenues to R&D—focused on hydrogen fuel cells for heavy-duty apps, 5G-enabled autonomy, and circular economy recycling for batteries. Recent tuck-in acquisitions like a telematics software firm enhance our services moat, targeting 50% aftermarket mix by 2027. Risks include interest rate sensitivity in construction and commodity volatility, but our diversified backlog and 42% services gross margins provide buffers.

I'll dive right into our total order intake, which came in at $2.85 billion for the quarter, representing a robust +18% year-over-year growth from $2.42 billion in Q3 2023. This marks our ninth consecutive quarter of double-digit order growth, underscoring the strength of our positioning in the industrial equipment market amid recovering capex cycles and the accelerating push toward automation and electrification.

To provide some color, core equipment book—encompassing CNC machining centers, precision assembly lines, and material handling systems—totaled $1.92 billion, up 14% YoY. This was driven by hyperscaler demand for semiconductor fabrication equipment, where we secured a landmark $450 million multi-year order from a leading foundry akin to TSMC for our next-gen AeroPrecision 5000 series wafer handling systems, optimized for 2nm node production. Additionally, EV battery gigafactory builds contributed $320 million, with notable wins from North American OEMs mirroring Tesla and LG Energy Solution, leveraging our modular FlexiBot AGV platforms with integrated battery management systems.

Aftermarket and services intake hit a record $930 million, surging +28% YoY, fueled by our expanding PredictiveEdge AI suite. This IoT-enabled predictive maintenance platform, now deployed across 15,000+ machines globally, saw uptake from wind turbine manufacturers like Vestas and Siemens Gamesa, who are retrofitting legacy fleets for higher uptime amid the IRA's clean energy incentives. Services now represent 33% of total intake, up from 28% a year ago, reflecting our strategic shift toward recurring revenue streams with 85%+ gross margins.

Regionally, Americas accounted for 47% of intake at $1.34 billion, +12% YoY, bolstered by CHIPS Act-funded fab expansions in Arizona and Ohio—think Intel's $20B Ohio megafab—where our book-to-bill ratio expanded to 1.22x. EMEA delivered $780 million or 27%, skyrocketing +32% YoY on the back of EU Green Deal capex, including €150 million in orders for hydrogen electrolysis equipment from Thyssenkrupp-linked projects. APAC contributed $730 million (26%), +15% YoY, with strength in China's solar PV and India's infrastructure push; however, we saw some softness in legacy automotive tooling due to slower-than-expected EV transition pacing at players like BYD.

Our ending backlog now stands at $6.2 billion, +24% YoY, providing exceptional revenue visibility—equivalent to over two quarters of trailing 12-month sales at current run rates. The overall book-to-bill ratio of 1.18x signals continued momentum into Q4 and FY25, well above our long-term target of 1.10x.

Strategically, this performance validates our TechForge 2025 initiative, where we've invested $250 million YTD in R&D for edge AI, digital twins, and sustainable manufacturing. For instance, our collaboration with NVIDIA on GPU-accelerated simulation for robotic welding systems has shortened design cycles by 40%, enabling us to outpace competitors like Fanuc and ABB in high-mix, low-volume production for aerospace OEMs such as Boeing. We're also capitalizing on supply chain reshoring, with 65% of our intake now tied to nearshoring trends versus 52% two years ago.

Looking ahead, we expect Q4 order intake to grow mid-teens YoY, supported by a $1.2 billion pipeline in electrification and semis, though we're monitoring macro headwinds like elevated interest rates curbing smaller-capex projects. Our disciplined pricing—up 4-6% across the board—combined with 20% YoY productivity gains from automation, positions us to convert this backlog at 98%+ fulfillment rates.

As we wrap up strong quarter results including adjusted EPS up significantly and record free cash flow, I'll now turn to our capital allocation priorities, specifically our ongoing share repurchase program. This remains a cornerstone of our disciplined approach to delivering shareholder value in the cyclical manufacturing and industrial equipment sector.

To recap, in January 2024, our Board authorized a $2.0 billion open-market share repurchase program over the next 24 months, superseding our prior $1.2 billion authorization from 2022, which we fully executed by Q4 2023. This new program reflects our confidence in Titan's long-term growth trajectory amid the global industrial upcycle, including the U.S. Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act fueling $1.1 trillion in domestic construction spend, Europe's REPowerEU initiative boosting demand for energy-efficient material handling equipment, and selective infrastructure plays in Southeast Asia offsetting softer volumes in mainland China due to their ongoing property sector deleveraging.

Through the end of Q3 2024, we have repurchased approximately $1.4 billion under the current program—that's 70% of the authorization in just nine months—acquiring 14.8 million shares at an average price of $94.60 per share. This represents about 5.2% of our diluted shares outstanding as of year-end 2023, reducing total shares outstanding to 272 million from 286 million at the start of the year. Post-repurchase, this delivers meaningful EPS accretion of roughly 5.5% on a trailing twelve-month basis, net of dilution from our employee stock purchase and long-term incentive plans, which issued 2.1 million shares YTD.

Our execution has been highly opportunistic and disciplined, leveraging automated Rule 10b5-1 trading plans established in Q1 to buy during periods of market volatility without market impact. For context, we accelerated purchases in Q2 when our stock traded at a compelling 10.2x forward EV/EBITDA multiple—well below the S&P Industrials index average of 12.5x and peers like Caterpillar at 13.8x or Deere & Co. at 11.9x—amid temporary headwinds from rising 10-year Treasury yields pressuring capex-sensitive end-markets. In Q3, we layered in $420 million at an average of $92.15, capitalizing on a 8% share price dip tied to broader industrials rotation out of cyclicals during the Fed's July pause.

Funding for these repurchases comes entirely from our industry-leading free cash flow conversion, which hit 115% of adjusted net income YTD at $1.85 billion. This FCF strength stems from operational leverage in our core segments: aftermarket parts and services now at 42% of revenue (up from 38% last year), pricing actions averaging 4.2% across our portfolio, and supply chain normalization reducing inventory days from 92 to 78. We've maintained a conservative net debt to EBITDA ratio of 1.6x, preserving ample dry powder for bolt-on M&A in high-ROIC areas like factory automation robotics—think collaborative robots for automotive tier-1s—and electrification kits for our legacy diesel-powered wheel loaders.

Regionally, our repurchase cadence aligns with uneven but resilient demand trends. In North America, which drove 55% of Q3 bookings, we've bought back shares aggressively as backlog for construction equipment like our skid steers swelled 22% YoY. Europe benefited from our early-mover advantage in EU Stage V-compliant engines, with uptake in wind farm installation cranes amid the green transition. Asia-Pacific saw moderated activity as we navigate China's 15% YoY decline in heavy machinery imports, but offset by Vietnam and India's infrastructure ramps, where our precision milling machines are gaining share against Komatsu and Hitachi.

Strategically, this program underscores our commitment to total shareholder return in an industry where repurchases have averaged 2-3% of market cap annually for top-tier players like Cummins and Ingersoll Rand over the past five years. By shrinking the float, we're enhancing our ROE from 22% to an expected 24.5% by year-end, while signaling undervaluation relative to our mid-teens organic growth potential through 2027. This is anchored in secular tailwinds: the shift to autonomous material handling systems (our AutoGuide AGVs booked significantly up), battery-electric off-highway vehicles qualifying for IRA tax credits, and Industry 4.0 digitization with IoT-enabled predictive maintenance on our lathes and presses, targeting 95% uptime for customers like Boeing and Tesla Gigafactories.

Looking ahead, we expect to deploy the remaining $600 million opportunistically through 2025, with potential for Board expansion if FCF exceeds our guide—prioritizing buybacks over dividends given our yield and long streak of increases. We'll continue monitoring multiples against peers; at current levels around 11x, we're poised to act if we trade below that threshold.

Now, turning to order intake performance and backlog dynamics, which remain core indicators of our visibility into future revenue streams at Titan Industrial Equipment Corp., a leader in precision industrial equipment including CNC machining centers, robotic automation systems, and heavy-duty material handling solutions. Order intake came in strong, exceeding guidance and marking robust growth year-over-year on an FX-neutral basis. This was driven by strength across key verticals: automation systems grew significantly, fueled by demand for our next-gen collaborative robots with integrated AI vision systems, while our semiconductor fab equipment surged amid the ongoing chip shortage and CHIPS Act investments. Aerospace orders contributed solidly as OEMs ramp narrow-body production.

Regionally, the Americas led, benefiting from reshoring trends and IRA clean energy incentives boosting orders for our wind turbine assembly lines. EMEA was challenged by energy headwinds, but APAC grew steadily with stimulus in China and bright spots in India for EV battery assembly equipment.

Our book-to-bill ratio expanded notably, reflecting pricing power on value-added features like IoT-enabled predictive maintenance and market share gains from our ModuForge platform, which reduces lead times compared to competitors. Backlog ended at a record level, up significantly year-over-year, with strong visibility: a good portion scheduled short-term, most within 12 months. This provides a hedge against regional softness.

On conversion rates, we're focused given supply chain normalization. Recent conversion improved, and we expect acceleration aided by dual-sourcing for critical inputs. Drivers include technical investments like digital twin technology across production lines, cutting cycles dramatically, and supply chain resilience with localized suppliers reducing exposure.

Strategically, we're capitalizing on Industry 4.0 tailwinds, with smart factory solutions comprising a larger share of intake as end-markets pursue digital transformation. We're also seeing pull-forward from sustainability mandates driving demand for low-emission equipment.

For the next quarter, we guide order intake to a healthy range, with book-to-bill sustained above benchmarks. Full-year should land strong, supporting raised revenue guidance. Risks include interest rates and China semis softening, but upside from reshoring and emerging pipelines like hydrogen equipment.

Finally, on our outlook for end market growth in the near and medium term, which underpins our guidance for fiscal 2025 and beyond. Our portfolio spans core industrial equipment segments for OEMs across key sectors. We're positioned at the intersection of traditional capex cycles and the secular shift toward digitalization and electrification.

In the near term—fiscal 2025 and into early 2026—we anticipate modest but resilient growth across end markets, with overall industry demand expanding at 3-5% globally. Semiconductor and electronics should see the strongest rebound, with fab expansions boosting demand for our machining and handling systems. Automotive and EV production growth tempered but offset by gigafactory ramps. Construction and mining mid-single-digits on infrastructure pipelines, agriculture challenged but with precision tech upside.

Regionally, North America leads, Europe moderates, Asia-Pacific bifurcated with India surging. Gross margins expand on pricing and productivity.

In the medium term—2026 through 2028—we see acceleration to 6-8% CAGR. Secular themes like electrified machinery ramp to a significant sales share, capturing ESG premiums. End-market specifics sustain strength in semis, rebound in ag, mining on supercycles.

Strategically, capex on automation hubs and M&A like our recent robotics acquisition. FCF funds returns. Risks include tariffs and slowdowns, but backlog and aftermarket moat protect.

We are committed to maintaining a strong balance sheet and generating consistent cash flow.

Now, I will hand over to David Ramirez, COO, for an operational update.

David Ramirez (COO):
Thank you, Lisa. Operationally, we've been focused on optimizing our supply chain, improving manufacturing efficiency, and enhancing customer service. Building on the backlog strength Lisa outlined, our conversion rates are accelerating to high levels through investments in dual-sourcing and digital tools, ensuring we fulfill orders at superior rates. We are leveraging data analytics to identify areas for improvement and drive operational excellence, including scaling digital twins and AI for faster production ramps. We are also investing in employee training and development to build a highly skilled workforce, particularly in automation programming and sustainable practices.

And I will turn the call over to our CTO, Dr. Elena Vasquez, for an update on our technology roadmap.

Dr. Elena Vasquez (CTO):
Thank you, David. We are committed to driving innovation and developing cutting-edge solutions for our customers. We are investing in research and development in areas such as artificial intelligence, machine learning, and the Internet of Things. We are developing solutions to improve predictive maintenance and optimize our customer's operations. I'm thrilled to dive into our Automation and Digital Offerings segment and its transformative impact on operational efficiency. Our segment delivered standout results, surging significantly year-over-year and representing a growing share of total revenue. Recurring revenue from SaaS platforms and predictive maintenance subscriptions hit records, with impressive EBITDA margins driven by high gross margins on digital services.

Customers are achieving ROI-proven gains: our flagship IndusEdge IoT platform delivers reductions in downtime, energy savings, and throughput improvements. For example, a major automotive OEM rolled out our system across plants, slashing repair times via real-time monitoring and ML models.

On robotics, our cobot lineup saw strong unit growth, part of end-to-end solutions enabling productivity gains amid labor shortages. We've launched Digital Twins as a Service, cutting prototyping time dramatically.

Regionally, North America turbocharged by reshoring, EMEA by green mandates, Asia-Pacific the star on policy pushes. R&D up focusing on generative AI, alliances with key partners. We guide strong growth ahead, with tailwinds from industrial AI forecasts.

Our new FlexiBot AGV platform is exceeding expectations, with significant impact on customer throughput and our recurring revenues.

Operator:
Thank you. We will now begin the question-and-answer session. Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith (Goldman Sachs):
Good morning. Can you discuss the trends you are seeing in automation spending?

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Good morning, John. Automation spending trends are robust, aligning with the growth in our segment that Lisa and I touched on. Customers across automotive, semis, and manufacturing are prioritizing it to combat labor shortages and boost efficiency. We've seen 30%+ order growth in cobots and IoT solutions, with deployments yielding 20-25% productivity gains. Reshoring and CHIPS Act are key drivers in North America, while EU Green Deal fuels EMEA. Our platform integrations are key, and we expect continued acceleration as rates ease.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Lee with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Mike Lee (JPMorgan):
What is your strategy for managing inflation and rising input costs?

Lisa Chen:
Thanks, Mike. Our strategy mirrors the margin drivers I outlined: hedging 70% of exposure, diversifying suppliers to reduce China reliance, and leveraging digital tools for productivity. Raw materials like steel are hedged, and we're passing through 4-6% pricing. Labor via internal automation, akin to peers. MarginPlus initiative targets leverage, and aftermarket mix buffers. We're confident in the guide even if costs stay elevated.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Chen with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Emily Chen (Morgan Stanley):
Can you provide an update on your efforts to reduce your carbon footprint?

Mark Thompson:
Thanks, Emily. Sustainability is core, integrated across ops. Through ElectriFlex pilots, battery-electric equipment, and $50M in recycling capex for EU CBAM and IRA. Scope 1 reductions via autonomous low-emission trucks, Scope 2 via efficient motors. MineConnect and AgriDigital cut energy use. Targeting hybrids/electrics at 20% construction sales by 2027, green steel positioning. Progress aligns with ESG mandates driving orders.

Operator:
Thank you. There are no further questions at this time.

Mark Thompson (CEO):
Thank you for your questions and your interest in Titan Industrial Equipment Corp. We are pleased with our progress this quarter and remain focused on executing our strategy and delivering long-term value for our shareholders.

Sarah Johnson (Head of Investor Relations):
Thank you, everyone, for joining us today. This concludes our earnings call. Have a great day.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for participating. You may now disconnect.
